questions.question: What device types text into a computer?
questions.explanation: Keyboards input text and commands.

questions.question: What device points and clicks?
questions.explanation: Mice control cursor movement and selection.

questions.question: What produces physical copies of documents?
questions.explanation: Printers create hard copies of digital files.

questions.question: What captures images and video?
questions.explanation: Webcams record video and take pictures.

questions.question: What converts physical documents to digital?
questions.explanation: Scanners digitize paper documents.

questions.question: What outputs sound and audio?
questions.explanation: Speakers play audio from computers.

questions.question: What displays large images for presentations?
questions.explanation: Projectors display content on screens.

questions.question: What records audio input?
questions.explanation: Microphones capture sound for recording.

questions.question: What touch-sensitive input surface replaces a mouse?
questions.explanation: Touchpads provide cursor control on laptops.

questions.question: What allows drawing directly on screens?
questions.explanation: Styluses enable precise digital drawing.

questions.question: Which device acts as both an input and an output device?
questions.explanation: A touchscreen displays output while simultaneously accepting touch input, making it a hybrid I/O device.

questions.question: Which printer type uses pins striking an inked ribbon to form characters?
questions.explanation: Dot matrix printers are impact printers that press pins against a ribbon, which is why they can still print multi-part carbon copies.

questions.question: What display technology do e-readers like the Kindle use to mimic paper?
questions.explanation: E-ink reflects ambient light like real paper and consumes power only when the page content changes.

questions.question: Which connector carries both high-definition video and audio over a single cable?
questions.explanation: HDMI transmits uncompressed digital video and audio together, unlike the analog VGA standard.

questions.question: Which output device produces large-format line drawings such as blueprints?
questions.explanation: Plotters draw continuous lines with pens or precision mechanisms, making them ideal for engineering and CAD output.

questions.question: Which device reads pencil-shaded bubbles on exam answer sheets?
questions.explanation: Optical Mark Recognition (OMR) readers detect marked positions on forms and are widely used for automated test grading.

questions.question: Which bulky display technology used a cathode ray tube before flat panels became standard?
questions.explanation: CRT monitors fired electron beams at a phosphor-coated glass tube, making them heavy and deep compared with flat panels.

questions.question: Which pointing device has a ball rolled by the fingers while its base stays still?
questions.explanation: A trackball works like an inverted mouse: the user rolls the exposed ball while the device itself remains stationary.

questions.question: Which output device produces raised-dot characters for visually impaired users?
questions.explanation: Braille embossers strike heavyweight paper to form raised dots that can be read by touch.

questions.question: Which device reads the embedded chip on ID and bank cards?
questions.explanation: Smart card readers access the integrated circuit on chip cards to authenticate users and process secure transactions.

questions.question: How do inkjet and laser printers differ from dot matrix printers?
questions.explanation: Inkjet and laser printers are non-impact devices; they form images without physically striking the page.

questions.question: What is a single device that prints, scans, copies, and faxes called?
questions.explanation: Multifunction printers (MFPs) combine several document functions in one unit to save space and cost.

questions.question: Which round 6-pin connector attached keyboards and mice before USB became standard?
questions.explanation: PS/2 ports were the standard keyboard and mouse connectors on PCs before USB replaced them.

questions.question: Which input device captures a handwritten signature for digital receipts?
questions.explanation: Signature pads digitize pen strokes so handwritten signatures can be attached to electronic documents.

questions.question: In mice and scanners, what does DPI measure?
questions.explanation: Dots per inch describes a scanner's optical resolution or a mouse's tracking sensitivity to movement.

questions.question: Which technology lets shoppers pay by tapping a card or phone near a terminal?
questions.explanation: Near Field Communication enables secure contactless exchanges between devices within a few centimeters.

questions.question: For competitive esports, which pair of monitor specifications matters most?
options: High refresh rate and low response time
questions.explanation: High refresh rates show more frames per second and low response times prevent ghosting, giving players faster visual feedback.

questions.question: A home user prints about 30 pages of text per week and wants sharp output without ink cartridges drying out between uses. Which printer type fits best?
questions.explanation: Laser toner is a dry powder that cannot dry out, and it produces crisp text at a low per-page cost for light duty.

questions.question: A drawing tablet advertises '8,192 levels'. What does this specification describe?
questions.explanation: Pressure levels measure how finely the stylus distinguishes pen force, letting artists vary line thickness and opacity.

questions.question: Which output device gives blind users tactile, changeable text to pair with a screen reader?
options: A braille embosser that prints each page once
questions.explanation: Refreshable braille displays raise and lower pins electronically to show screen text line by line, unlike a one-time embossed page.

questions.question: A photographer wants gallery-quality color prints at home. Which printer technology delivers the widest color range for photos?
questions.explanation: Photo inkjets blend many ink colors, producing smooth gradients and wide gamuts that lasers and other types cannot match.
